title: Mask and reveal sensitive account, path, and identifier values in operational UI
description:
Problem: the continued live review found several operator surfaces showing full account identifiers, linked sign-in identifiers, local filesystem paths, and long audit targets by default. This is useful for debugging but noisy in normal use and risky for screenshots, demos, shared browser sessions, and copied reports.

Desired outcome: operational screens should default to privacy-conscious summaries while preserving copy/reveal affordances for operators who need exact values.

Scope:
- In scope: Profile linked sign-in methods, Admin Users/OAuth/Audit/History/Variables, Health runtime configuration, local path values, account/user identifiers, email-like identifiers, and copy/reveal affordances.
- Out of scope: changing persisted audit records, authentication identifiers, or diagnostics API payload contracts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sensitive-looking identifiers and local paths are masked or summarized by default in UI.
- Exact values can be copied or revealed intentionally with clear affordances and accessible labels.
- Tables remain scannable after masking, with stable columns/card labels.
- Browser screenshots of default operator views avoid exposing full account emails, user IDs, or local machine paths.

Validation:
- Capture Profile, Admin Users, Admin Audit, Admin Variables, and Health before/after using generic fixture or masked values.
- Run focused browser checks for reveal/copy behavior and accessible names.
- Ensure no persistence or API contract behavior changes unless explicitly intended.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from 2026-05-25 continued live review: Profile/Admin/Health surfaces displayed full local paths and account or target identifiers by default. Task text intentionally avoids copying real observed values.
